question: Δ RST is an obtuse isosceles triangle with m∠R = 16° and m( {overline {TR} } ) > m( {overline {ST} } ) . What is the measure of ∠S?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **isosceles triangle** ΔRST, two angles must be equal. Given **m∠R = 16°**.

Condition **TR > ST** implies angle opposite to TR must be greater than angle opposite to ST.

∴ **m∠S > m∠R**, so m∠S cannot be 16°.

If equal angles are m∠R = m∠T = 16°, then **m∠S = 180° − (16° + 16°) = 148°**.

Since 148° > 90°, it satisfies the **obtuse** condition.

**∴ The correct answer is 148°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ΔRST is **obtuse isosceles** triangle.

m∠R = 16°

m(TR) > m(ST)

**Formula Used:**

Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°

Side-Angle Inequality: The side opposite to the **greater angle** is longer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/603b6e17d57ddf0a0e810ef8906cbddce54d0d7d4bd2ae3985b53f3ad26afe4c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In ΔRST, the side **TR** is opposite to ∠S and side **ST** is opposite to ∠R.

⇒ Given TR > ST ⇒ **m∠S > m∠R**

⇒ Since m∠R = 16°, we must have m∠S > 16°.

⇒ For an **isosceles triangle**, two angles must be equal. Possible cases for (m∠R, m∠S, m∠T):

⇒ Case 1: If m∠S = m∠T, then 16° + 2 × m∠S = 180° ⇒ 2 × m∠S = 164° ⇒ m∠S = 82°. (Triangle is 16°, 82°, 82° which is **acute**, so rejected).

⇒ Case 2: If m∠R = m∠T = 16°, then m∠S = 180° − (16° + 16°) = 148°.

⇒ Here 148° > 16°, which satisfies the condition m∠S > m∠R (TR > ST).

⇒ Also, 148° > 90°, making the triangle **obtuse**.

**∴ The correct answer is 148°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle-Side Relationship

In any triangle, the side opposite to the largest angle is the longest side, and the angle opposite to the longest side is the largest angle.

Obtuse Isosceles Triangle

A triangle where one angle is greater than 90° and two sides (and their opposite angles) are equal. The equal angles must always be acute.

Sum of Angles Property

The interior angles of any Euclidean triangle always sum up to exactly 180°.</p
